editorial.summary: A 3:05 JRE #1965 derivative in which an interviewer asks why Africa draws the storyteller back. He contrasts expression/creation with professional art’s business and monetization, recounts arriving with an important-artist ego and art supplies, drawing with children near a cave, imagining museum/archive/book/donation futures for their work, then watching drawings discarded after a hunting party returns. He interprets the act as presence and impermanence, throws away his own carefully made drawing and wants less anxiety about editing and money. Every insight and uncomfortable outsider phrase remains, including real-men/hunting, raw/untrained children, material-nonpossession and happiness claims. Those are attributed perceptions, not anthropology. The record establishes no exact itinerary, community consent, ownership, publication, sale, donation, causal happiness claim, representative Hadza view or exact spelling for three closing private names. Supported cave/wind/mini repairs improve meaning; one hunter phrase stays unclear and zero turns are named.
